title: How a Solar Panel Works in 60 Seconds ☀️⚡ #shorts
description:
A solar panel has no moving parts. Sunlight knocks electrons loose inside layers of silicon, an electric field pushes them into metal contacts as direct current, and an inverter turns it into AC for your home. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#solarpanel #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: A solar panel has *no moving parts*, yet it turns sunlight straight into electricity.

steps.label: Cells
steps.text: Each panel is a grid of *silicon cells* under protective glass.

steps.label: Two Layers
steps.text: Every cell has two silicon layers, *n-type* on top and *p-type* below. Where they meet, an electric field forms.

steps.label: Photons
steps.text: Sunlight is made of *photons*. When one hits the silicon, it knocks an *electron* loose.

steps.label: Current
steps.text: The field pushes those electrons into thin metal contacts. That flow is *direct current*.

steps.label: Inverter
steps.text: An *inverter* changes DC into AC, the kind your home outlets use.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Light in, *electrons* out. Follow Inside 60 for more.
